newsitem.title: USA: IKON Office slips amid UK sales uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: IKON Office slips amid UK sales uncertainty.

text.p: Ikon Office Solutions Inc slid after the company said it may take up to 12 months before sales in Britain return to the "previous run rate," analysts said.
Ikon, which provides total office solutions, dropped 3 to 25-1/2 in heavy trading.

As part of its second quarter earnings report, Ikon Office said second quarter revenues from the United Kingdom declined "significantly" from a year ago, hurting internal revenue growth by 2.5 percentage points. Total internal revenue growth for the second quarter was 11.5 percent, the company said.

"UK operations are continuing to recover from an abrupt and untested consolidation in the first quarter. Since then, management changes were made, the organization is being rebuilt, and IKON expects the UK to return to previous run rates within the next 12 months," the company said in a statement.

Ikon Office posted second-quarter operating earnings of $0.37 a share, up from $0.31 a share a year ago. Including transformation costs, second quarter net income was $0.07 a share, compared to $0.50 a share a year ago. Second quarter revenues grew 26 percent to $1.3 billion.
Separately, Ikon said that its president, Kurt Dinkelacker, was named to the additional post of chief financial officer.
Robert Kearns, currently chief financial officer, becomes senior vice president of finance. He will oversee financial and accounting changes affecting the newly created customer service centers.
Ikon's "transformation" program, which began last year, has been accelerated to be completed a year earlier in October 1998.
